questions.question_summary: Apple-style product judgment should balance user experience, accessibility, privacy, performance, and implementation quality.
questions.generated_question: A feature improves engagement but makes the interface more complex and may reduce accessibility for some users. How would you evaluate whether to ship, redesign, or delay it?
follow_up_strategy: Ask how the candidate defines product quality beyond engagement.
Probe accessibility, privacy, performance, and user trust trade-offs.
Ask what prototype, test, or user signal would change the decision.
Check whether the candidate can protect craft while still making a decision.

questions.question_summary: Apple iOS/frontend signals emphasize platform depth, implementation quality, performance, and user-facing polish.
questions.generated_question: You are improving a mobile screen that feels slow and inconsistent across device sizes. Walk me through how you would diagnose the issue, improve implementation quality, and verify the user experience.
follow_up_strategy: Ask how the candidate separates layout, rendering, network, and state-management causes.
Probe performance measurement and platform constraints.
Ask how they test accessibility and device variation.
Check whether code quality and user perception are both considered.

questions.question_summary: Apple-style craft often requires cross-functional collaboration without lowering quality standards.
questions.generated_question: Tell me about a time you had to protect product quality while working with partners who had different priorities. What did you do and what changed?
follow_up_strategy: Ask what quality bar was at risk.
Probe how the candidate aligned design, engineering, product, or operations partners.
Ask what trade-off was accepted and why.
Check whether the result improved user experience or product reliability.

questions.question_summary: Apple product design patterns should test user problem framing, critique, iteration, and platform-quality trade-offs.
questions.generated_question: Choose a product experience you would redesign for clarity and accessibility. How would you identify the core user problem, explore alternatives, and decide the final direction?
follow_up_strategy: Ask what evidence shows the current experience fails users.
Probe design alternatives and trade-offs.
Ask how accessibility and platform consistency are evaluated.
Check how feedback from engineering and users changes the design.

questions.question_summary: Apple AI/ML role signals should test evaluation quality, privacy, on-device constraints, and user usefulness.
questions.generated_question: A model performs well in offline tests but requires more personal data and device resources than expected. How would you evaluate whether the model belongs in the product?
follow_up_strategy: Ask how the candidate defines user value and acceptable resource cost.
Probe privacy-preserving alternatives and on-device constraints.
Ask how offline evaluation maps to real product quality.
Check whether the candidate proposes monitoring or fallback behavior.

questions.question_summary: Apple fit should connect motivation to product craft, values, and role-specific contribution, not brand admiration alone.
questions.generated_question: What specific kind of product problem or craft standard makes Apple the right environment for you, and what evidence from your past work shows you can contribute to that standard?
follow_up_strategy: Ask for a specific product or user problem rather than general Apple admiration.
Probe role-specific depth and past evidence.
Ask how the candidate handles feedback and high quality bars.
Check whether values like privacy or accessibility are naturally connected where relevant.
